'''Kano Shrine''' (蚊野神社, *Kano Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the [[Kōtai Jingū]] (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in {{ill|Tamaki|en|Tamaki|qid=Q1289593|lt=Tamaki}}, {{ill|Watarai District|en|Watarai District|qid=Q1131032|lt=Watarai District}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}, Japan. It holds the 7th Rank among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine.<ref name="uy">Ujiyamada City Hall, ed. (1929): pp. 9–11.</ref>

This article also covers '''Kano Gozen Shrine''' (蚊野御前神社, *Kano Gozen Jinja*), which is enshrined alongside Kano Shrine.

Both shrines are dedicated to deities protecting the tributaries of the Sotokida River.<ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p. 68.</ref>

== Overview ==

This section covers information common to both shrines.

Located at 1807 Kanosatonaka, {{ill|Tamaki, Mie|en|Tamaki, Mie|qid=Q587348|lt=Tamaki, Mie}}, [[:en:Watarai District, Mie|Watarai District]], {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}.<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p. 60</ref> The area of Kano, where the shrines are situated, lies within a rural landscape, with {{ill|Kano Shrine|ja|蚊野神社}} and {{ill|Kano Shrine|ja|蚊野神社|lt=Kano Gozen Shrine}} enshrined within a large forest in the local settlement.<ref name="gk"/>

The shrine grounds cover an area of 8,383 m².<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Research Association (1990): p. 196</ref> In ancient times, the shrine grounds spanned approximately 2 chō (≈19,834 m²).<ref name="jg">Fukuyama et al. (1975): p. 150</ref> The precincts are covered with moss.<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 64</ref>

The shrine buildings are constructed in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|en|Shinmei-zukuri|qid=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri}} style with board roofing, facing south.<ref name="sk6"/> A single-layered {{ill|Sacred fences|en|Tamagaki|qid=Q3078312|lt=tamagaki}} fence with a gate surrounds the shrine, and a single {{ill|Torii|en|Torii|qid=Q234731|lt=Shinmei torii}} stands at the entrance.<ref name="sk6"/>

== Kano Shrine ==

Kano Shrine is an auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine of Ise and enshrines a {{ill|Mirror|en|Mirror|qid=Q35197|lt=mirror}} as its sacred object.<ref name="th">Kaneko (1983): p. 59</ref> It is affectionately known as "Kanamori-san."<ref name="gk"/><ref name="ic"/> In ''Daijingū Gishiki Kai,'' Nakagawa Tsunemasa explains that "Kanamori" is a corruption of "Kano Mori," and the shrine’s name derives from the name of the area where it is located.<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Research Association (1990): p. 195</ref>

The enshrined deity is Ōkami Mikagekawa no Kami (大神御蔭川神).<ref name="gk"/><ref name="ic"/> This deity is considered the god of a tributary of the Sotoda River, which flows through the Kano area,<ref name="ic"/> and is revered as a local development god.<ref name="gk"/> The same deity is enshrined at {{ill|Mifune Shrine|ja|御船神社 (多気町)}}, another auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine.<ref name="th"/> The ''Jinmyōchō Kōshō'' identifies the deity as {{ill|Seoritsu-hime|ja|瀬織津姫命|lt=Seoritsuhime}} and interprets the name Ōkami Mikagekawa no Kami as "the spirit of {{ill|Amaterasu|abstract|Q455602|ar|أماتيراسو|ary|أماطيراسو|az|Amaterasu|bcl|Amaterasu|be|Аматэрасу|be_x_old|Аматэрасу|bew|Amatérasu|bg|Аматерасу|ca|Amaterasu|cs|Amaterasu|da|Amaterasu|de|Amaterasu|el|Αματεράσου|eo|Amaterasu|es|Amaterasu|et|Amaterasu|eu|Amaterasu|fa|آماتراسو|fi|Amaterasu|fr|Amaterasu|gl|Amaterasu|he|אמטראסו|hi|अमातेरसु|hr|Amaterasu|hu|Amateraszu Ómikami|hy|Ամատերասու Օմիկամի|id|Amaterasu|it|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|jv|Amaterasu|ka|ამატერასუ|ko|아마테라스 오미카미|la|Amaterasu|lb|Amaterasu|lt|Amaterasu|lv|Amaterasu|min|Amaterasu|ml|അമതേരസു|mni|ꯑꯃꯇꯦꯔꯁꯨ ꯑꯣꯃꯤꯀꯃꯤ|ms|Amaterasu|nl|Amaterasu|nn|Amaterasu|no|Amaterasu|or|ଆମାତେରାଶୁ|pa|ਆਮਾਤੇਰਸ|pl|Amaterasu|pt|Amaterasu|ro|Amaterasu|ru|Аматэрасу|sco|Amaterasu|sh|Amaterasu|simple|Amaterasu Ōmikami|sk|Amaterasu Ómikami|sl|Amaterasu|sr|Аматерасу|su|Amaterasu|sv|Amaterasu|ta|அமதெரசு|th|อามาเตราซุ|tl|Amaterasu|tok|jan sewi suli Amatelasu|tr|Amaterasu|uk|Аматерасу|uz|Amaterasu|vi|Amaterasu|wuu|天照大神|zh|天照大神|zh_min_nan|Amaterasu|zh_yue|天照大神|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}}, purifying sins by the river."<ref name="sk6"/>

In ancient times, the shrine hall was specified to be 10 shaku (≈3.03 m) in length, 9 shaku (≈2.73 m) in width, and 5 shaku (≈1.52 m) in height, with an altar measuring 4.5 shaku (≈1.36 m) by 2.5 shaku (≈0.758 m) and 1 shaku (≈0.303 m) in height. The shrine was surrounded by a sacred fence (mizugaki), gate, and tamagaki.<ref name="jg"/>

== Kano Gozen Shrine ==

Kano Gozen Shrine is Ranked 8th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine, following Kano Shrine.<ref name="uy"/> The main hall has been discontinued, and the deity is now enshrined together with Kano Shrine.<ref name="uy2">Ujiyamada City Office (1929): p. 10</ref>

The enshrined deity is Gozen no Kami (御前神).<ref name="ic"/> The ''History of Ujiyamada City'' refers to this deity as "Kano Gozen no Kami."<ref name="uy2"/> Similar to the deity of Kano Shrine, this deity is considered the god of a tributary of the Sotoda River.<ref name="gk"/> Gozen no Kami is regarded as the deity who calms and supports Ōkami Mikagekawa no Kami.<ref name="tm"/>

In ancient times, the shrine had an independent hall measuring 3.5 shaku (≈1.06 m) in length, 2.4 shaku (≈0.727 m) in width, and 7 shaku (≈2.12 m) in height.<ref name="jg"/>

== History ==

According to the ''Taijingū Shiki,'' the shrine was established during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|en|Emperor Yūryaku|qid=Q357235|lt=Emperor Yūryaku}}.<ref name="sk5"/> It was designated as one of the shrines to be rebuilt every 20 years alongside the main shrine, with officials assigned to oversee the reconstruction.<ref name="sk5"/> 

During the {{ill|Middle Ages|en|Middle Ages|qid=Q12554|lt=medieval period}}, the rebuilding process became irregular. For example, during the reconstruction on the 30th day of the 12th month in {{ill|Bun'ei|en|Bun'ei|qid=Q1010103|lt=Bunei}} 3 (Julian calendar: January 26, 1267), the Gozen Shrine, its gate, sacred fence, and torii were not rebuilt. The last clear record of reconstruction was on the 8th day of the 12th month in {{ill|Ryakuō|en|Ryakuō|qid=Q1146182|lt=Ryakuō}} 3 (Julian calendar: December 27, 1340), when materials from {{ill|Kaga Province|en|Kaga Province|qid=Q907469|lt=Kaga Province}} were ordered for the rebuilding.<ref name="sk5"/>

On September 7, {{ill|Kanbun (era)|en|Kanbun (era)|qid=Q1146228|lt=Kanbun}} 3 (Gregorian calendar: October 7, 1663), thanks to the efforts of the Chief Priest {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}}, the shrine was restored at its current location.<ref name="sk5"/> A site survey before the restoration confirmed the presence of post holes and decayed pillars, identifying the site as the old shrine grounds.<ref name="sk6"/> There were no objections to the decision to restore the shrine at this location.<ref name="sk6"/>

The shrine buildings were rebuilt in October {{ill|1916|en|1916|qid=Q2087|lt=1916}} (Taishō 5).<ref name="uy2"/>

== Rituals ==

During the {{ill|Kinensai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinensai}}, {{ill|Tsukinamisai|ja|月次祭}} (in June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}}, {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|en|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518|lt=Niinamesai}}, and temporary festivals, rituals are performed by priests in front of the shrine.<ref name="sk5"/> For the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}, {{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭}}, National Foundation Day Festival, {{ill|The Emperor's Birthday|ar|عيد ميلاد إمبراطور اليابان|az|İmperatorun ad günü|de|Geburtstag des Kaisers|es|Tennō tanjōbi|eu|Enperadorearen urtebetetzea|fa|روز تولد امپراتور|fr|Fête nationale du Japon|he|יום הולדתו של הקיסר|id|Hari Ulang Tahun Kaisar|it|Tennō tanjōbi|ja|天皇誕生日|ko|천황탄생일|ms|Hari Keputeraan Maharaja|nl|Verjaardag van de keizer|pl|Urodziny cesarza Japonii|ru|День рождения императора|si|අධිරාජයාගේ උපන්දිනය|th|วันพระราชสมภพของสมเด็จพระจักรพรรดิ|tr|İmparatorun Doğum Günü|uk|День народження імператора|vi|Sinh nhật Thiên hoàng|zh|天皇誕生日|qid=Q72318}}, and Wind Day Prayer Festivals (in May and August), remote rituals are conducted at the Gojōden of the Inner Shrine.<ref name="sk5"/>

== Surroundings ==

The {{ill|Kumano Saigoku Kaidō|ja|熊野西国街道}} passes nearby, with remnants of pine tree-lined paths still visible.<ref name="gk"/> Additionally, many ancient Kofuns have been discovered in this area, including 19 kofun in the Bōzu-yama Kofun group.<ref name="sk6"/>

* Approximately a 20-minute walk from {{ill|Tokida Station|eo|Stacio Tokida|ja|外城田駅|jv|Setatsiyun Tokida|ko|도키다역|ur|ٹوکیڈا اسٹیشن|zh|外城田站|qid=Q7813584|lt=Sotoda Station}} on the {{ill|Sangū Line|en|Sangū Line|qid=Q872023|lt=Sangū Line}} operated by {{ill|Central Japan Railway Company|en|Central Japan Railway Company|qid=Q513679|lt=JR Central}}.<ref name="tm"/>
